Subject: Staged evidence sprint + orderlink orchestration (MSA/DPA/order form)

Alicia / Daniel —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our call I attached a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP_AsterBiotics_v1.xlsx) and the current MSA+DPA draft (Redwood_MSA_DPA_draft_v2.docx). High-level proposal here: we split acceptance and order activation into two milestones so procurement can sign the order form to reserve capacity while DPA evidence gates run in parallel.

Proposed runway (high-level):
- Week 0: Order form signed (activation hold: billing starts on milestone completion or 30 days, whichever earlier)
- Week 1–3: Evidence sprint (SOC2 artifacts, retention proofs, SIEM checklist) — minimal items required for data ingestion
- Week 4: Conditional acceptance + feature flag lift for production traffic

Key asks from your side: a named procurement contact for DocuSign, and legal counsel who will review the MSA/DPA redlines. I flagged three clauses in the draft that we recommend fast-track: data residency appendix, incident notification SLAs, and audit window.

If that sequencing looks right, can we book a 30-min alignment on Monday (9/7) to lock owners and sign-off windows? I copied Karthik and Laura to confirm internal readiness on evidence turnaround and legal redlines.

Attachments: MAP_AsterBiotics_v1.xlsx, Redwood_MSA_DPA_draft_v2.docx

—Grace

Grace — thanks for the materials and the clear runway. A couple of procurement/finance questions before we lock the 30-min sync: 

1) If we sign the order form on Week 0, will billing be conditional on conditional acceptance (i.e., do you cap invoices until evidence gates complete)? We need explicit language for our finance team.
2) For the evidence sprint: can you confirm the expected ownership for SOC2 artifact delivery vs. Redwood-provided evidence (e.g., runtime logs, audit API)? Our security team (cc'd Priya) will need to sign off on which artifacts are customer-provided vs. vendor-provided.
3) Proposed acceptance window: what is Redwood's escalation path if evidence isn't available by Week 3? We prefer a fallback that doesn't cause immediate billing but also doesn't freeze onboarding indefinitely.

Priya — looping you in on the MSA/DPA draft. Can you flag anything obvious in the redlines that would change the sequencing?

We can make Mon 9/7 at 11:00am PT work for a 30-min call, or Tue 9/8 if that helps with internal alignment.

Thanks,
—Daniel

Subject: Re: Staged evidence sprint + orderlink orchestration (MSA/DPA/order form)

Daniel — quick answers below, and I attached a one-page evidence checklist (evidence_checklist_vA.pdf) that maps artifacts to owner and expected delivery window.

1) Billing / finance: We are comfortable with a conditional billing clause. Typical language we use is: "Billing commences on the earlier of (a) 30 days after Order Execution or (b) successful completion of Conditional Acceptance as defined in Section X." If you prefer billing paused until completion, we can add a temporary credit hold but we'd need a clear remedial timeline (eg +30 days) to avoid open-ended capacity.

2) Evidence ownership: In the checklist: Redwood provides runtime logs, uptime reports, and an audit API export. Customer provides identity/access reviews and any local retention attestations we can't produce. We've flagged SOC2 in-scope artifacts that Redwood can provide (policy copies + SIG review) versus items Aster must attest to.

3) Escalation / fallback: Our recommended fallback is a staged remediation plan: 7-day remediation window with an auto-escalation to MAM (Customer Success + Account Exec) and a late evidence plan that grants a 15-day provisional production allowance under a limited support SLA. That keeps the onboarding moving without immediate invoicing changes.

Proposed next steps:
- Lock owners on the evidence checklist (see attachment)
- Laura to provide annotated MSA redline positions for the three fast-track clauses by EOD Wed 9/8
- If Aster is OK with the conditional billing language above, we can issue an updated order form + DocuSign link by Thu 9/9

I can own the finance language and Ben can own the order-form technical appendix. Grace, will you coordinate the 9/7 or 9/8 sync?

—Karthik
